Hello everyone. I would like to ask your guys' input on my old martial arts school:(http://karate4u.com/)) as well as your own experiences and thoughts on Mcdojos in general. There will be a part 2.

Here's how it all started:I started at King's Martial Arts when the Karate Kid remake came out. Like those who grew up with the original, it made me want to do martial arts. If you look at their website you see that they have programs in Morgan Hill and Gilroy which was at a community center. Me and my sister went there for a few months but then we moved to San Jose. After quite awhile I went back but it turns out they also had a school at a church but one of the instructors(the pastor's son) was scamming us and took more money from my mom's account. We switched to the San Jose school(as you can see by now it was a chain) and that's where the post starts off. At the time I was 13.

So first off what I would like to say that I'm 100% certain that this was a Mcdojang. It had just about all of the signs which i will show. First off, many serious martial artists understand that full contact, free-form fighting is something that is needed at some point in one's training to develop stamina, reflexes and the ability to take punishment. But this was not the case at this dojang:(https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=46EQnGbhUag))

So as you could see in the video here were the red flags in terms of sparring:

-You had to purchase the gear through the school only. The full gear set cost $200 for all the pads and stuff. When i was going to this studio when i lived in San Jose(almost two years ago), i bought a sparring set for $110 dollars due to the high price of the studio. But I was only allowed to use it once which brings me to my next point...

-I couldn't use the sparring set because the only difference between it and the set sold by the school was that the gloves and footpads didn't cover the fingers and toes. Now this isn't a problem for non-Mcdojo schools but here they told me i couldn't wear it for insurance reasons and whatnot. Now you may be thinking, ''Well they want the class to be safe and no one wants to be sued,'' but here's the thing...

-As you also heard in the video, the sparring was LIGHT contact, no head contact, no face contact, no grappling, they even say in the video that if someone's hitting you harder than light you should tell them to stop(it's one thing if a person is a beginner and you up the contact as they go but to do this for the entirety of one's training will get you killed in the street.)

Now this is why it upsets me to this day. You're paying 200 bucks for a helmet, foot pads, arm pads, leg pads, and a torso protector, but you can't even hit remotely hard or aim for the face/legs in the first place. And even if you did get them in those areas by accident, you are hitting them LIGHTLY. And if you didn't have pads you couldn't spar you would just punch the bags.

Secondly, when i was last there, I swear they had the infamous ''get a black belt in two years'' classes complete with special uniform, badges, etc. It seems they may have changed it to 6 years now, but I do know for a fact that when i was last there there were 12-13 year old black belts(keep in mind no full contact training, lot's of forms, complient techniques, we did POINT FIGHTING WITH FOAM WEAPONS AND HAD TO WEAR THE FULL GEARSET FOR CHRIST'S SAKE!

I do not remember the price a month but yeah this was definitely a mcdojo. I'm just sharing my experience, though. If you just want physical fitness or a sport then schools like this are fine for you. But if you are looking to know how to defend yourself and others, DO NOT GO TO SCHOOLS LIKE THESE! Thank you.

So what are your guys experiences with the dreaded Mcdojo? what's your opinionon them?
